name: Call Christmas Tree Spread (1x3, uncovered)
summary: Buy 1 ATM call and sell 3 further-OTM calls at one higher strike; the historical 'christmas tree', which leaves 2 uncovered short calls and unlimited upside risk.
when_to_use: INCLUDED FOR COMPLETENESS ONLY - DO NOT TRADE IN THIS SYSTEM. Historically used by floor traders with deep capital in very high IV. The 2 uncovered short calls create theoretically unlimited loss and require naked-call approval.
max_profit: net credit + (short strike - long strike) x 100, at the short strike
breakevens: lower = long strike - credit/100; upper = short strike + [(short - long) + credit/100] / 2

greeks.delta: positive at entry, flips sharply negative above the short strike

entry_rules: BLOCKED: requires Alpaca options level 4 (uncovered short calls). Level 3 accounts cannot and must not submit this. The automated system should reject this slug at the order-router layer.
If ever enabled: IV rank > 70, short strike delta <= 0.15, and a hard-coded buy-stop hedge in the underlying above the upper breakeven.
management_rules: N/A under Level 3. If enabled at Level 4: close at 50% of credit, and close unconditionally if spot trades within 0.5 x (short - long) of the short strike.
exit_rules: If ever enabled: ASSIGNMENT GUARD - 3 short calls, 2 of them naked; flatten by 15:45 ET on expiration day and immediately on any ITM short call with extrinsic < $0.10; close before every ex-dividend date when the short calls are ITM.
assignment_risk: Catastrophic. Three short calls, two of them uncovered: assignment creates a short stock position of 200 shares per unit with no offsetting long option, at any price. On an index ETF that is an unbounded liability.
buying_power: Naked short call margin on 2 contracts: roughly 20% of underlying value per uncovered contract plus premium, recomputed daily. A single SPY unit would tie up most of a $50k account.
common_mistakes: Confusing this with the 1-3-2 christmas tree BUTTERFLY, which is defined risk and Level 3 eligible. The system must keep the two slugs strictly separate.
zero_dte_notes: Absolutely not. Uncovered short calls at 0DTE on an American-style ETF are the fastest path to an assignment disaster.
family: three-leg-structures (butterflies, broken-wing butterflies, lizards, three-strike ratio spreads, ladders/tree spreads, christmas trees, and three-leg stock+option hybrids)
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
